dataset: NEC edition in force by state (49 of 51 jurisdictions verified on state or DC government pages; NYC listed separately)
attribution: Source: state code-adoption records as linked per state — retrieved Oct 2026
rules: Render only rows with status 'verified'. A row with another status (now HI, 'conflicting') stays in the file for its notes and is not rendered.

States in not_verified were checked but have no verified edition: list them as 'not verified', with no edition. HI: a newer NEC may have become the state code by default under HRS 107-24(c), and no state document says which edition or from when. MS: no state statement on electrical codes was found. A state with no row that is not in not_verified is 'not yet checked' (none at present).
Counts are per jurisdiction: distinct state codes, NY-NYC excluded and OH counted once, out of 51 (50 states and DC).
Never publish counts from the IAEI adoption table (undated; state records contradict it for several states, including AK, IL, MD and NV).
NFPA's enforcement map could not be read (JavaScript-only); do not cite it for any state value.
Local amendments and city codes can differ from the state edition; say so on the page.
Rows with edition 'local' mean no single statewide electrical code: render 'Local adoption' plus the scope text.

Show each row's scope text. Never drop it for AL (State Building Code only), KS (statewide fire-code NFPA 70, 2008 edition, beside local adoption), IL (NEC current or preceding edition where no local code exists) or NV (local adoption; State Fire Marshal codes without NFPA 70; state buildings on the 2023 NEC). OH has two rows (commercial and residential); key rows by state plus scope.
effective null means no start date was found: show no 'since' date.
next_change: with a date, say 'changes to the {edition} NEC on {date}'; without a date, say the {edition} NEC is proposed or pending, never a date.
TN: after the edition add 'per the State Fire Marshal's list updated April 17, 2025'; a July 2025 revision of rule chapter 0780-02-01 has not been read.

states.scope: Hawaii State Electrical Code as adopted by the State Building Code Council (2020 NEC with amendments). By statute (HRS 107-24(c)) a newer NEC edition may have become part of the state building code by default. County codes can differ.
states.source_publisher: Hawaii Department of Accounting and General Services, State Building Code Council (Hawaii State Electrical Code, effective March 15, 2022); conflict from HRS 107-24(c) and 107-25 as printed in 2025 bills
states.quote: “NEC” means the National Electrical Code, NFPA 70, 2020 edition, | Effective Date: March 15, 2022
states.note: Do not render an edition. Verified: the SBCC adopted the 2020 NEC effective March 15, 2022 (adoption notice of March 31, 2022, posted by the County of Kauai: 'adopted the 2020 NFPA, NEC on March 15, 2022'). Conflict (R5-1, 2026-10-24): HRS 107-24(c), as printed in 2025 bills S.B. 48 and S.B. 120, says 'If the council does not adopt a code or standard identified in section 107-25 within the two-year time period,' 'that code or standard shall automatically become part of the Hawaii state building code until superseded'. HRS 107-25(a)(4) (H.B. 745 and H.D. 1, 2025) lists 'The National Electrical Code, as published by the National Fire Protection Association;'. The rule is not limited to particular codes. SBCC minutes of July 21, 2020 record the same reading ('the national codes become the State Building') and 'DAG Kam confirmed this interpretation.' DAGS annual reports: no codes adopted in 2023, 2024 or 2025 (Governor's housing proclamations); December 2025: 'the 2021 model Codes for IBC, IRC, and IECC were adopted by default in the State'. No state document says whether, or from what date, the 2023 NEC became the state code by default; the date would be two years after its official publication date, which no state source read gives. No 2026 SBCC action on the NEC was found; 2026 bills and bill-status pages could not be read. County level: Hawaii County Code ch. 5D (SUPP. 18, 7-2025) still adopts 'The National Electrical Code, 2017 Edition'. IAEI pointer 3/14/2023 is the State-building date.
